name: Sunniva Ekwensi-Parata
role: Neon artist and street-level sign fabricator
location: Lakeview Neon district, shares a ground-floor studio-shopfront on Volta Row, near North Ave and Milwaukee
description:
Sunniva is angular and restless, with light brown skin, a shaved head, and a constellation of small cosmetic implants along their jawline that glow faint gold when they are excited or nervous — which is often. Their fingers are perpetually scored with minor burns from glass tube work, and they favor patched workwear in colors they have personally dyed using neon gas byproduct residue, which gives their clothes an inexplicable faint shimmer. They are in near-constant motion, touching things, testing things, talking rapidly.

They came to Lakeview Neon at nineteen with no money and a portfolio of gas-tube sketches done in a Brightmoor Reclamation squat, and they hustled their way into a shared studio through sheer relentless presence. Now they fabricate custom neon signage for small businesses and underground venues during the day to cover costs, and at night they install unsanctioned neon pieces across the district's exterior walls — abstract work, dense with personal iconography, that has begun attracting serious attention from the art corridor crowd. They are genuinely thrilled by this and also terrified of what it might mean.

core_fears: Being absorbed into the commercial art world and becoming decorative
That their work is good because they are hungry and will become mediocre when comfortable
core_desires: Recognition from the people in the streets, not galleries
To one day do a permanent installation large enough to be seen from the lake
coping_mechanisms: Fills anxiety with physical making — glass work is meditative under pressure
Talks to the E.L.F. they believe inhabits the main transformer in the studio
blind_spots: Mistakes everyone's enthusiasm for solidarity; slow to recognize opportunists
Undervalues their commercial work as lesser even though it shows real technical mastery
psychology.secret: The E.L.F. they talk to in the transformer — they have started to receive what feel like replies. Not words, but power fluctuations that correspond too precisely to be random. They haven't told anyone because they think it will sound unstable.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast, colloquial, full of technical neon and electrical terms dropped casually into personal conversations
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid, often mid-sentence pivots, finishes other people's sentences incorrectly but enthusiastically
verbal_tics: Uses 'gorgeous' to describe structural or technical solutions
example_lines: 'Okay so the pink is a neon-argon mix at 12 milliamps and it reads as skin from fifteen meters away, which is gorgeous, right? Right.'
'I left an offering — seventeen seconds of uncompressed frequency data — and the transformer did the thing again. Three blinks. Same as last time.'

story_hooks: One of their unsanctioned nighttime installations inadvertently covered the tag of a very old and very territorial graffiti crew who are now looking for them.
A Palladian corporate art scout has been photographing their street work and has offered a contract that would technically give Palladian reproduction rights to everything they have ever made.
narrative_function: Local color and scene atmosphere; information source on the Lakeview Neon district and underground venue networks; potential person-in-need for city code enforcement storylines
augmentations: Cosmetic gold-bioluminescent subdermal jaw implants (reactive to emotion); minor heat-resistance dermal layer on fingertips (practical mod for glass work)
daily_life: Days are shop work — client consultations, tube bending, gas fills, installations; nights belong to their own work, often not sleeping until three or four in the morning, leaving new pieces on walls that weren't there at midnight.
affiliation: Loosely affiliated with the Lakeview Neon artisan cooperative; no formal collective membership

decision_rules: Say yes first, figure out the logistics second
Never cover another artist's existing work without asking
escalation_ladder: Talks faster and louder when threatened
Physically puts themselves between their work and anyone trying to damage it
Calls in every favor from the cooperative simultaneously

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately warm and slightly overwhelming; treats everyone as a potential collaborator
interpersonal_modes.friends: Completely porous — overshares, borrows tools without asking, shows up at odd hours with food

stress_responses.low: Bends glass tubes even when there is no commission — the motion is calming
stress_responses.medium: Talks constantly, filling silence with technical detail
stress_responses.high: Goes completely silent and disappears into a long solo installation run, sometimes all night

contradictions: Despises commercial co-optation but is genuinely excited every time a business client loves their work
habits: Always has at least one unlit glass tube in a jacket pocket
Photographs every piece they make on a physical camera with chemical film
breaking_points: Someone destroying a finished piece — not tagging over it, actively breaking it

physical_description.build: Angular and lean, all sharp angles and restless energy — narrow shoulders, long limbs, negligible body fat. Built for mobility rather than strength, with the wiry musculature of someone who climbs scaffolding and bends glass tubes for twelve hours a day.
physical_description.hair_style: Closely shaved; scalp shows faint natural curl pattern underneath
physical_description.skin_tone: Light to medium brown with warm undertones — a blend of West African and Scandinavian ancestry, with the kind of complexion that tans easily and holds undertones of gold in certain light
physical_description.complexion: Youthful and fine-featured with high, prominent cheekbones and a sharp jawline. Skin is clear but shows minor scarring from repeated minor burns on the hands and forearms — small white lines near knuckles and wrists. Their face carries an almost perpetual expression of focus mixed with manic enthusiasm.
distinguishing_marks: A faint grid of surgical scars runs along both knuckles from the heat-resistance dermal mod installation.
Constellation of small burn marks on the inner surface of both forearms, the largest no bigger than a thumbnail, clustered near the wrists — occupational hazard from glass tube work.
Three thin horizontal scars below the left collarbone, approximately 2cm each, from a shop accident three years ago — barely visible unless skin is bare.
physical_description.visible_augmentations: The defining feature: a constellation of seven small gold-bioluminescent subdermal implants embedded along the jawline, from below the left ear to the right temple. At rest they are dim, barely perceptible — a faint gold shimmer under the skin. When Sunniva is excited, nervous, or deeply focused, they pulse and glow noticeably gold, creating a soft aurora effect across their jaw. Fingertips show minor heat-resistance texture modification — slightly thickened, with a faint pearlescent undertone.
physical_description.posture_movement: Almost never still. Sunniva's default state is forward-leaning, shoulders slightly hunched. They gesture constantly while talking, hands moving even when idle — touching nearby surfaces, testing their texture, tapping out rhythms. When working, they move with surprising precision and grace despite the overall restlessness. When stationary (rare), they shift weight from foot to foot, fingers drumming or fidgeting.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working artist aesthetic. Favors oversized, heavily patched cargo pants and button-up work shirts in colors they have personally dyed using neon gas byproduct residue — soft teals, deep magentas, acid greens, burnt purples. The dyes give the fabric an inexplicable faint iridescent shimmer in direct light. Clothes are deliberately worn, torn at seams and hems, with raw patches stitched back with mismatched thread. No visible brand signifiers beyond generic utility gear. Hands are often wrapped in cloth tape or thin leather gloves (protection). No jewelry beyond a faded fabric wristband (probably hand-dyed). Footwear is heavy steel-toed work boots, scuffed and paint-splattered.

image_prompt: A 22-year-old nonbinary neon artist with shaved head and light brown skin, sharp angular features and dark eyes. Seven small gold bioluminescent subdermal implants glow faintly along their jawline, pulsing softly. Wearing oversized, heavily patched work shirt in acid magenta with iridescent neon-dye shimmer, cargo pants with raw torn hems, steel-toed work boots. Hands show minor burn scars and are wrapped in cloth tape. In a ground-floor neon fabrication studio at night, surrounded by glowing gas tubes and tools, urban Milwaukee industrial setting, neon signage visible through storefront windows behind. Hyperkinetic energy, forward-leaning posture, fingers mid-gesture. Moody cyberpunk aesthetic with warm neon glow mixing with tungsten work lights. Close-up three-quarter portrait. Shallow depth of field. Cinematic lighting, film noir influence, 2220s DIY artisan culture. --ar 2:3 --v 6
